p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: Content templates must be customized and installed before traffic setup to ensure message alignment with your store positioning.
1. Go to Shopify Admin. 2. Click Discounts. 3. Click Create discount. 4. Select Amount off order. 5. Set discount type to Percentage. 6. Set discount value to 5%. 7. Use discount code SAVE5. 8.
Apply to all customers. 9. Do not set a minimum purchase requirement. 10. Do not set usage limits. 11. Do not set an end date. 12. Save the discount.

1. Go to Sales Channels > Online Store > Themes. 2. Click Edit theme. 3. Switch page view from Home page to Products. 4. Select Default product template. 5. Expand Product information in the left sidebar. 6.

Click the eye icon next to Expiring coupon to enable it. 7. Update the text to "5% Off All Orders". 8. Enter coupon code SAVE5. 9. Set expiration to 3 days. 10. Choose a theme color matching your brand. 11.

Use Month/Day/Year date format for US sales. 12. Save changes.
1. Log in to your Shopify Admin.
2. Click Apps.

3. Search for 'Shopify Messaging' in the App Store.
4. Select Shopify Messaging (best match).
5. Click Install.

6. Approve required permissions.
1. Open Shopify Messaging settings.
2. Click Template branding.

3. Select Customize.
4. Upload your store logo.
5. Choose your store font (default sans-serif is acceptable).

6. Keep email background and text simple.
7. Set button fill color to match your brand.
1. Go to Shopify Settings.

2. Click Notifications.
3. Set sender email to sales@yourdomain.com.
4. This address will be used for all Shopify Messaging emails.
Access abandoned checkout automation: Shopify Admin → Shopify Messaging app → Create automation → Select template 'Recover Abandoned Checkout' → Turn on automation.

Edit the workflow in Shopify Flow via Marketing → Automations → Install Shopify Flow.
1. Open the Shopify Inbox app.

2. Click "Turn on chat" to open the theme customizer.
3. Choose a widget color to match your brand.
4. Change the text color and button color.

5. Select an icon (chat bubble, smiley, hand wave, etc.).
6. Keep the widget positioned in the bottom-right.

7. Customize the greeting text (e.g., "Welcome to [Store Name]" with an offer to help).
8. Save changes in the theme customizer.
9. Refresh your storefront.

10. Confirm the chat icon appears.
11. Send a test message to yourself.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: Use the Manhattan Shopify theme to create email capture pop-ups for bounced visits, and configure Shopify Email to deliver the follow-up automation.

1. Log in to Shopify Admin.
2. Click Apps.
3. Search for 'Judge.me'.
4. Select Judge.me Product Reviews app.
5. Install the free plan.
To customize review branding: Open Judge.me settings → Branding → set the primary color to match your store. This color will appear on stars in review emails and widgets.
To position the Review Widget: Go to Online Store → Themes → Edit theme → switch to a product page → find the Review Widget under Apps → drag and drop to position.
Recommended placement is under the product description.
On the homepage, create a prominent box labeled 'Your cart is ready' that (1) displays the customer's current cart items; (2) shows the total cart value;
(3) includes a single 'Continue to checkout' button to re-engage browsers who navigated away from the cart after adding items.

On cart pages, add a product recommendation section labeled 'You May Also Like' that (1) displays curated product options; (2) includes zoom buttons allowing customers to view product images at larger
size without leaving the cart page; (3) includes add-to-cart buttons that add items immediately without navigating away; (4) rank products by best-selling items.
To configure the Charlotte theme's email popup on Shopify, navigate to the admin dashboard, go to Online Store > Themes > Customize, open the gear icon menu, and find Email Pop-up Settings.
Activate the popup toggle, enable logo upload and add your store's logo, and set the popup to appear after 60 seconds.
Enter your discount code, write the heading as 'wait, don't leave us', and use the body text 'enter your email below to receive a special discount from [Store-Name]'.
Leave the countdown timer disabled since it's unsuitable for this campaign. Set the button copy to 'send me the discounts', adjust colors to match your site's branding, and save the changes.
The Shopify Email automation sequence for welcome messages works identically regardless of how you collect the initial email address.
You can use Charlotte's built-in popup, any third-party popup app, a landing page form, or any other collection method-the downstream automation flow remains the same.
You are not locked into one theme or tool; focus on collecting the email and the automation takes over from that point.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: Aftership is used as a tracking website for order tracking notifications.
Shopify Email is sufficient for promotional email marketing; Klaviyo is not necessary as an additional expense.
Coupon code bar location: Shopify admin > Online Store > Theme Settings > left navigation panel > find Coupon Code Bar section > enable/disable as needed.
If the 'Recover Abandoned Checkout' template does not appear first in the Shopify Messaging app templates list when creating an automation, search for it by name using the search field.

1. Create new Zapier Zap named 'AC to Slack' or similar. 2. Select Shopify as trigger app and choose 'New Abandoned Cart'. 3. Authenticate Shopify account and select store. 4. Confirm delay set to 0 hours. 5.

Add action: send Slack channel message. 6. Authenticate Slack and select channel (e.g., #steve). 7. Insert customer fields (name, phone, order total, checkout URL) using Zapier's field insertion tool. 8.
Save and activate Zap.
Use large typography for a headline announcing that customers receive a free bonus item with their product purchase. Display a photograph of the bonus product and state its retail value in dollars.
Confirm that this complimentary item is automatically included with purchases made at your store.
An organic store should look professional, branded and simple, with a short purchase path. Avoid stacking pop-ups that force visitors to close windows, although a single email signup is acceptable.
For reviews on a product page, add many more reviews as view counts grow, since visible social proof is expected to improve conversion. Place the review block right after the description.
For products on an organic-only collection, use promotions to the email list and social audiences rather than paid traffic. Products under the normal ad threshold can be sold this way.
Bonjoro integrates directly with Shopify.
When a new order is placed, the customer's name and email are sent to Bonjoro and appear in a daily list of thank-yous to record, so the team does not need to look up details in Shopify.
Scribeless integrates directly with Shopify and pulls the customer's shipping address from the Shopify order. The note is then packaged and mailed automatically without manual address entry.
Video thank-yous need only a webcam or phone camera with a built-in microphone. A professional microphone is unnecessary, and headphones with an inline mic can be used as well.
Holiday site banner pattern: a seasonal sale headline plus a coupon code that the customer enters at checkout. Formula: [Holiday] sale, enter coupon code [CODE] to check out.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: The code is unique to the holiday, so you can track its sales, and the banner catches first-time visitors from paid ads. Example 1: Winter sale, enter coupon code WINTER20 to check out.

Example 2: Summer sale, enter coupon code SUNNY15 to check out.
Setting up a holiday sale on the store:

1. Create a coupon code that is unique to the holiday sale.
2. Add the sale to the homepage image slider.

3. Show a banner strip across the whole site with the sale name and the coupon code.
4. Check that first-time visitors from Google Ads will see the banner.
5. Link the sale to a dedicated collection page with all the holiday offers.
Create one dedicated collection page for the holiday offers and send all emails and remarketing ads there. Do not link them to the homepage or to a single product page.

Create the pop-up coupon in Shopify:
1. Go to Discounts in the Shopify admin and click Create discount.
2. Select Amount off order.

3. Enter the discount code and name (example: save five).
4. Set the value as a fixed amount of $5.

5. Set the usage limit to one use per customer so the code cannot be reused repeatedly.
6. Click Save discount.
Add a short product quiz when the catalogue is large, so visitors who feel overwhelmed by choice get a recommended product after a few questions.

Create the expiring discount code in the Shopify admin:
1. Open Discounts in the sidebar of the Shopify admin.
2. Click Create discount code.

3. Enter the code name, for example save 10.
4. Choose the discount type Percentage.
5. Enter 10 as the discount value for 10%.

6. Keep all products selected and apply it to all products in all collections.
7. Leave minimum requirements unset.

8. Set customer eligibility to everyone.
9. Leave usage limits unset.
10. Leave the end date empty; a start date may be set.
11. Click Save discount code.
Do not set an end date on the Shopify discount itself, because these codes are recycled in later cycles. The deadline is controlled through the announcement bar text instead.
All bundle items must sit in one Shopify collection, and that collection must be the Applies to target of the automatic discount.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: A collection that holds only part of the bundle will leave some items without the discount.

Countdown timers should not be added at launch, because they only make sense once the store is generating sales. Add them later as part of conversion work, not as a standard element of the first test.
Personalization in Klaviyo emails: use Add personalization to insert the customer's first name, last name or email address into the text.
Mistake: hiding the free gift or offer until add-to-cart on mobile, so visitors do not see the offer before the cart; state the free gift or offer on the product page itself.
Create an automatic buy X get Y discount in Shopify: Discounts > Create discount > choose Buy X get Y > name it (for example 'Buy 2 items
and get the third one for free') > choose Automate discount > set the quantity condition (buy 2 items of a specific collection) > set the free item from the collection > Save discount.
Communicate a discount on a Shopify collection page: 1) Open the collection in Shopify. 2) Edit its description. 3) Add the offer text as a large headline or just above the logo.
4) Format it, for example as Heading 3 and in a clearly visible color. 5) Save the collection page and refresh the store page to confirm the offer shows.
A buy-X-get-Y offer must be checked against the margin: if the product is high-ticket (for example above $100), giving an item free may not make sense, so the calculation must always work
and the store must make profit.
The cart and checkout should show the same offer as the one promised on the website and in the ads, including the discounted price and the free item, so customers see the same deal at every step.
A store with several pop-ups, especially pop-ups stacked on top of each other, pushes shoppers away. Limit pop-ups.

Editing or removing a coupon bar in the Source A Shopify theme:
1. Open the Shopify admin.
2. Go to Online Store.

3. Click Theme settings.
4. Open the coupon code section and edit the offer, for example to 5% off or free shipping.
Do not delete the coupon bar entirely, because it helps conversions. Change the offer instead, for example to 5% off or free shipping.
Judge.me is the recommended review app for Shopify because of its deep integration; reviews appear on product pages automatically and star ratings can show in Google Shopping ads.
Judge.me is a Google-approved partner and its reviews show in Google Shopping.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: Use a free live chat widget that only opens when a visitor clicks a small button in the corner, instead of intrusive pop-up offers; full-screen pop-ups usually look messy on laptops and are not recommended.
Upfront product pricing matters: a store needs a clear offer and a reasonable price for its products, and overpriced items without a bundle can hurt conversion.
A poor offer, such as a single item priced high without a bundle or compelling deal, can lower conversion. Test different offers and price points before scaling.

Modify the store so visitors see the active offer:
1. Promote the offer in the notification bar.
2. Promote the offer in the exit intent overlay.
3. If the offer needs one (for example a bundle), create a custom product page for it.
4. If the offer needs one (for example an entered-to-win offer), create a content page that explains the offer details.
5. If the offer needs one (for example a bonus offer), edit the current product pages to show the offer.
6. If the offer needs one (for example spend X to get X), use Bold Sales Motivator to show how far the shopper is from the free bonus.
Install a one-click upsell app such as Zipify on Shopify so that the post-purchase page shows a one-time offer before the regular thank-you page.
The upsell should be a different product, not a bundle of the original, and priced at or below 14 dollars, because higher prices can hurt conversion.
Add a Messenger opt-in to the product page so visitors can subscribe to messages when they add to cart.
This lets abandoned cart messages reach them through Facebook Messenger instead of only email.

Product review apps should display reviews only when you have permission. Use reviews provided by the supplier. Do not copy reviews from competitors' sites, since they can report the store and cause a suspension.
A supplier's reviews can be used on your product pages when the supplier gives permission. Suppliers often do not collect reviews themselves because they rely on retailers for marketing.
Enable product reviews and product ratings only after the store has about 50 product reviews, because some eligibility requirements depend on a minimum number of reviews.
Promotions can be enabled earlier.
Use countdown timers only for real promotions with an end date, such as a monthly promotion or a Black Friday or Cyber Monday sale, and not as a permanent feature.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: An order-tracking app can add an order tracking page to the store, using a code provided by the app. Look for a tracking option that does not slow down the store.

Shopify email to add SMS is coming; SMS apps are not needed for a new store at the start.
Steps to produce and deliver the ebook bonus:

1. Generate the full ebook text with Claude (claude.ai) using the ebook prompt.
2. Copy the generated content.
3. Paste it into Canva and apply a simple ebook template.

4. Export the design as a PDF.
5. Upload the PDF to Shopify.
6. Deliver it automatically with every order.

1. Open the Digital Downloads app and select the product you use as the free gift (for example a product named e-book).
2. Click Add asset, then File.

3. Upload the PDF file that was generated for the ebook.
4. Confirm the file appears under Assets.
5. Open the product page and go to the Shipping section.

6. Tick Not a physical product so the order carries no shipping.
7. Click Save.
8. In the bundle, attach this product as the free gift for bars 2 and 3 and confirm it is available.

Judge.me widget color is set in the app under Settings, by opening the review widget section and using the color picker. Choose the store's main brand color so the stars and widget match the color scheme.
A Shopify theme does not sell digital products by itself.
For free bonuses, you can deliver links to PDFs or unlisted videos without an app, and paid digital products need a Shopify app that handles automated delivery.
The chat button appears in the bottom right corner of the store by default, on both mobile and desktop.
The recommended button style is the plain chat icon only, which saves space and is recognizable without text.
Chat greeting example used in the store: "Hi, message us with any questions. We're happy to help." This text can be set as the welcome message in the chat settings.
On Shopify Plus, Checkout Plus can be shown in the cart and in checkout, and the shopper can change the choice in checkout, using Shopify's checkout extensibility.
Without Shopify Plus, it only shows in the cart and the choice cannot be adjusted in checkout. Package protection has the same limit.
Checkout Plus is set up as a product in Shopify, so it appears on the order. Shopify Markets allows a different price per market, and the offer does not have to run in every market.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: Setting up a branded tracking page with Wonderment: 1. Use the Wonderment block provided for Shopify. 2. Create a new page the same way as a collection, product or about-us page. 3.
Insert the tracking block on that page. 4. Add subscriptions, upsells or cross-sells to the page. 5. Send customers to this page instead of the carrier's tracking page.

Shopify forced a migration of the thank-you and order status pages, and these pages can hold tracking blocks, upsells and cross-sells. Treat them as a sales channel instead of leaving them at the default setup.
Create a dedicated loyalty program page on the Shopify store with the program details. Link it in the footer and/or the main navigation so customers can find it while browsing.
Optionally add a link to the page on product pages, though this takes space and is not required.
Use a tracking tool called After Ship for order status. Logged-in customers can see their order status on the site.
Place reviews on product pages, ideally on the products that already get impressions and clicks, because those are the pages shoppers already view. A store-wide review page is an acceptable fallback.
The review date display and review images are controlled by your review app, not by the theme. Look for date or image options in the review app's settings.
Add a personal thank-you and a point-of-contact line to the default Shopify order confirmation template rather than sending a separate follow-up email. This covers both messages in one email.
A page on a Shopify store can show product-specific supplier reviews only with written supplier permission.
Enter them through the review app on the product page rather than copying or screenshotting them.
Customize and reuse supplier reviews: get the supplier's permission first, then enter the review manually in the Judge.me app as if a customer had written it. Judge.me uses no automation here.

Shopify Inbox setup for live chat: enable it in the Shopify admin; install the Shopify Inbox app to receive messages on the phone; to pause chat on the site, disable the chat box in the Shopify Inbox settings.

The built-in pop-ups, cross-selling and social proof features are meant for stores that already get traffic and sales. A demo store still being built does not need them and should not spend time on them.

A Shopify store can take sales without any customer ratings or reviews, so reviews are not required before launch.
Hi [Supplier name],
We have just uploaded your products to our website and want to show our customers that they are high quality. Is it okay for us to use the reviews from your website?

If you have reviews you could send us, we would appreciate it.
Thank you, [Your name] [Company name]
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: Do not import product reviews from Amazon, because those reviews belong to Amazon. Reviews from a supplier's own website can be used after asking the supplier for permission.
Build the lead generation landing page as a Shopify page with a small amount of code, or use the free version of PageFly, a landing page builder for Shopify.
The page usually sits at a store URL such as yourstore.com/freebook.

Shopify admin > Store > Theme settings is where the store's coupon code and promotion text are edited in the theme. If the option is not visible in the left navigation, check the theme settings path in the admin.
Hidden add-on products are created in Shopify but left out of every collection and kept out of search. They are shown only as upsells or add-ons through an upsell app such as Bold Upsell.
Do not set up discount banners or coupons until the store is live, sending traffic, and has products ready to sell. Before that point they have no effect.
Set the live chat app to show a greeting such as asking the visitor for their question and email address, or hide the chat widget when no one is available.
Embedded email opt-in page with Klaviyo: 1. Create a sign-up form inside Klaviyo. 2. Copy the embed code Klaviyo provides. 3. Create a new page in Shopify. 4.
Paste the embed code into that page so new sign-ups are tagged and can trigger automations.
The current Shopify theme does not have a built-in opt-in code. If no email tool provides an embed form, a third-party Shopify app is needed to place a sign-up form on a page.
The automatic shipping confirmation email to the customer is only sent if the "send a confirmation to the customer" tick box is checked in the Fulfil Items popup.
If the box is left unticked, the customer gets no fulfilment notice and must be contacted manually.
The Shrine theme includes a built-in quantity discount feature. Use it to offer multi-unit deals on a product test store instead of building a separate bundle page.
Expiring coupon (discount code) block in the product information section: it shows discount codes that switch on and off based on dates.
For a demo store, keep it disabled or hidden; hide it with the eyedropper icon instead of deleting it.
Sale banner image block: it shows a sale message and a discount code at checkout. It is not needed for a demo store and can be hidden.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t:
Install the Q&A app on the product page:
1. Install the app from its listing and accept the permissions it requests.

2. Click Add questions and answers when the app offers to add itself to the store.
3. In the product page template, add a section to the page.

4. Choose Apps in the section list, then select Questions and answers.
5. Click Save, and check a product page on the live store to confirm the section appears.
1. In the left navigation under Template, click the arrow next to Product information to expand the section.
2. Hover over the Expiring coupon entry and click the eye icon to make it visible again, since it was hidden when the demo products were uploaded.

3. Click Expiring coupon so its settings open in the right-hand panel.
4. If the right-hand panel does not appear, zoom out in the browser until it shows.

Preparing the store for each promotion window:
1. Replace the notification bar with the current offer.
2. Swap the exit-intent overlay to show the offer.
3. Create a custom product page for a bundle, or modify the existing product page if the offer is small.
4. For an event, create a content page with the details and eligibility rules.

5. Add a progress tracker such as Bold Sales Motivator if the offer depends on a cart threshold.
6. Update the promotions page with the offer, if you use one.
Keep one static promotions page and swap its content when a promotion starts, since this is easier to remove later.
Bundles and bonus gifts should get their own page, so they can be removed without affecting the rest. Event pages that may rank in search can stay live and later become evergreen content.

Closing a promotion, done manually after the window:
1. Set the notification bar back to the default offer.
2. Restore the previous exit-intent overlay.
3. Remove bundle or bonus content from product pages and return them to their default state.
4. Replace the offer on the promotions page with the default offer or the next offer.
5. Turn off progress trackers such as Bold Sales Motivator, so no shopper reaches a goal that unlocks nothing.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: Show the same holiday message on every promotional placement during the promotion: the homepage image slider, the announcement bar, and the expiring discount code section on product pages.
Change them when the promotion changes.
Rebuy's Shopify Functions discounting currently supports Free Product, Order Discount and Fixed Price tiers.
It works on all Shopify plans, Basic, Advanced and Plus, while Shopify Scripts require the Plus script editor.
Adding a tracking page with AfterShip on a Shopify store: 1. Install the AfterShip app from the Shopify app store. 2. AfterShip sends automated tracking emails to customers. 3.
Copy the embed code that AfterShip provides and place it on a store page, which then works as the order tracking page where customers enter their tracking number.

1. In the Shopify admin, open Apps and then Visit the Shopify App Store.
2. Search for talk to and open the tawk.to Live Chat app.
3. Click Install app. Shopify lists the data the app can view and manage (orders, customers, online store); approve it, because the app cannot work without it.
4. You are redirected to a tawk.to page. Click Sign Up and create a new account, then complete the standard sign-up process.
5. At the Install Widget step, do not paste the tracking code. Open the list of platforms, select Shopify, then click Done.
6. Return to the Shopify app, log in with your tawk.to account, select your widget (the name entered during sign-up) and click Use selected widget.
7. Confirm the success message and open the storefront to check that the chat bubble appears at the bottom of the screen.
8. Adjust the widget appearance in the tawk.to settings (see the widget appearance setting).

Shopify includes built-in email marketing for follow-up emails to buyers and to visitors who leave without buying, as well as automatic order tracking so customers can follow their shipment until delivery.
Shopify Admin > Discounts lists every discount created by Functions.
Product tier discounts appear with the name and type Rebuy Product Discount, and order tier discounts with Rebuy Order Discount. The admin name never matches the text shown at checkout.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: All product tiers of one Smart Cart are grouped into one single Rebuy Product Discount in Shopify Admin, so adding a second product tier does not create a second discount.

Likewise, all discount tiers are grouped into one Rebuy Order Discount.
Create a standard order discount code in the Shopify admin:

1. Open the Discounts section in the Shopify admin. No discounts exist by default.
2. Click Create discount.
3. Choose Amount off order.

4. Select discount code instead of automatic discount.
5. Enter the code name, for example save 10.
6. Choose percentage (the usual choice) or fixed amount, and enter the value, for example 10%.
7. Under minimum requirements, enter a minimum order value such as 2000, or leave it at no minimum.

8. Under customer eligibility, restrict the code to specific customer segments if needed.
9. Set maximum discount uses: 5 total, 10 total, or once per customer, or leave it unlimited.

10. Keep the combination with other promotions turned off.
11. Keep the start date at the current date and time, or set a later start.

12. For a time-limited promotion, set an end date.
13. Click save discount.
Shopify offers four discount types: amount off products, amount off order, buy X get Y, and free shipping. Amount off order is the type used most often for order-level discount codes.
A demo store does not need discount codes. Create them once the store is live and taking real orders.

On the Shopify checkout page, the customer sees a discount code field, enters the code, and clicks apply. In the demo, a 10% code gave a 319.60 dollar discount, which implies an order subtotal of about 3196 dollars.
A store can hold as many discount codes as needed, and all of them are listed together in the Discounts overview.
This allows one-off codes for individual buyers to be managed alongside general promotions.

Test a discount code on the storefront before sending it to a buyer:
1. Add a product to the cart on the store.

2. Open the cart and go to the checkout.
3. In the discount code field on the checkout page, enter the code.
Further details (continued)
p.s: Discounts, offers, email capture and post-purchase

p.t: 4. Click apply and check the discount amount that appears for the order.
On-site upsell positions are: (1) on the product page, shown before Add to cart; (2) on the cart page, shown before checkout (pre-checkout upsell); (3) after payment
but before the thank-you page (post-checkout upsell), which inserts an extra page into the checkout flow.
Shopify checkout supports at most two levels of post-purchase upsells; after two offers the customer must land on the thank-you page.

Post-purchase structure (the monster funnel), in order:
1. The customer buys the main item and completes payment.
2. Show the first upsell.

3. If accepted, show the second upsell; if declined, show the first downsell.
4. If the second upsell is accepted or declined, show the thank-you page.
5. If the first downsell is accepted, show the thank-you page; if declined, show the thank-you page.
Shopify checkout allows at most two levels of post-purchase upsells, so you cannot show three or four offer pages before the thank-you page.
Plan the funnel with a maximum of two offers plus a downsell path.

Enable a post-purchase funnel in Shopify under Settings > Checkout. Scroll down to the post-purchase page section and select Reconvert upsell and cross-sell. The page may take a while to load after the change.
Change post-purchase discounts under Discounts and shipping in the upsell app. You can switch the discount between percent and fixed amount per unit, change the timer, and edit the button text.
A gift card of 80 Swiss francs was sold, and buyers received a code by email. Around Christmas, three to five gift cards were sold, many of them were never redeemed, and that amount became revenue.
Gift cards sold poorly outside peak gifting periods but can add revenue during Christmas.
Create an automatic discount in the Shopify store so that when two specific products are both added to the cart, one of them is given free. The customer does not need a code.

Do not show a review widget that states a product has no reviews. A visible zero-review signal (negative social proof) suggests nobody has bought it or that it is not good, so hide the widget until reviews exist.
Most Shopify review apps allow the widget to be hidden when a product has zero reviews.
